questions.label: Is this included in the evaluated service?
questions.description: Record the named package boundary. Add-ons and partner delivery are not included service.
questions.example: Reactive hunting is included; proactive hunting requires an add-on.

questions.label: Where can the service receive cases and evidence?
questions.description: Separate incoming alerts from direct telemetry and customer requests.
questions.example: We ingest SIEM incidents, query EDR evidence directly and accept employee-reported phishing.

options.label: Directly from EDR, NDR, identity or other detection tools
Employee reports or custom investigation requests

questions.label: Can you operate over the customer's existing SIEM?
questions.description: State whether the SIEM stays in place and who operates it.
questions.example: The customer keeps its SIEM; we consume alerts, query evidence and write back case updates.

options.label: Yes, we operate or co-manage their SIEM
SIEM is not required or used

questions.label: Who connects and maintains sources?
questions.description: Include connector maintenance and missing-telemetry handling, not just initial setup.
questions.example: Our team maintains shipped connectors; custom sources require customer engineering.

questions.label: Can employees or the SOC submit custom investigation requests?
questions.description: Include suspicious activity that did not generate an alert.
questions.example: An employee reports an unusual MFA prompt through Teams and our analysts investigate.

questions.label: Who or what performs this work?
questions.description: Distinguish provider humans, deterministic automation, ML and LLM or agent reasoning.
questions.example: An LLM proposes queries, integrations execute them, and an analyst approves containment.

questions.label: How are the provider's humans involved?
questions.description: Provider oversight is separate from customer delegation or approval.
questions.example: The customer pre-authorizes containment, but a provider analyst approves each execution.

options.label: Runs within policy; human supervises and can intervene

questions.label: Customer work, limits and evidence
questions.description: Describe required customer work, dependencies, exceptions and a redacted evidence reference.
questions.example: The customer connects identity sources and approves actions on privileged accounts.

questions.label: Is this included in the evaluated service?
questions.description: Record the named package boundary. Add-ons and partner delivery are not included service.
questions.example: Reactive hunting is included; proactive hunting requires an add-on.

questions.label: Where do you develop and maintain detections?
questions.description: Distinguish provider-owned detections from detections deployed into customer tooling.
questions.example: We tune rules in the customer's SIEM and maintain our own cross-customer detection content.

questions.label: Can customers inspect and change detection logic?
questions.description: Describe actual permissions, not just visibility of detection names.
questions.example: Customers can read the rule, request changes, and export it; they cannot edit production rules directly.

options.label: View and export, changes by request
Changes by request; logic not visible

questions.label: Which threat hunts do you deliver?
questions.description: Reactive hunts follow an incident; proactive hunts do not require an existing alert.
questions.example: We hunt after escalations and run campaigns based on new threat intelligence.

questions.label: How are hunt findings tracked?
questions.description: Explain whether campaigns have owners and actions through to completion.
questions.example: Each campaign links findings to detection changes with an owner and completion status.

options.label: Campaigns, findings, owners and follow-up actions

questions.label: What context do you gather?
questions.description: Include security history and business context; avoid claiming sources only available through custom work.
questions.example: We use previous incidents, identity privileges, asset owners and business criticality.

questions.label: How is context stored or retrieved?
questions.description: A graph, database or live lookup can all be valid. Describe the implementation rather than its marketing name.
questions.example: Relationships are stored in a graph; historical case text is retrieved from a vector index.

options.label: Live queries without a persistent context store

questions.label: How is customer context kept accurate?
questions.description: Who refreshes it and can the customer correct it? Explain stale or conflicting evidence in the optional details.
questions.example: Connectors refresh asset records daily and customers can correct asset criticality.

options.label: Automatic refresh; corrections via our team

questions.label: Can you use customer history from before onboarding?
questions.description: Distinguish importing historical cases from searching older telemetry.
questions.example: We import previous case decisions and search retained SIEM logs when new indicators emerge.

options.label: Import history and run retrospective checks

questions.label: What investigation work is delivered?
questions.description: Choose the work the service actually performs, not every capability of an underlying tool.
questions.example: Our team builds a timeline, hunts for related activity and determines affected identities.

questions.label: Can you interact directly with employees?
questions.description: Explain channels, identity verification and privacy controls in the details below.
questions.example: Our analyst contacts the employee through an approved Teams channel to confirm activity, with the conversation linked to the case.

options.label: AI-assisted messages reviewed by a human
AI interacts directly within approved boundaries

questions.label: What DFIR support is available?
questions.description: Collection alone is not a full forensic investigation. Include evidence integrity and chain-of-custody limits in the details.
questions.example: Artifact collection is included; full forensic analysis requires a separate retainer.

questions.label: Where can the service execute response actions?
questions.description: Receiving alerts from a tool does not establish the ability to take action in it.
questions.example: We can isolate endpoints and revoke identity sessions, but only recommend network changes.

questions.label: Where does your responsibility end?
questions.description: Choose the normal contracted boundary; describe exceptions below.
questions.example: We contain the threat and verify containment; the customer owns rebuilding affected systems.

questions.label: How does the customer authorize response?
questions.description: Customer delegation is separate from whether your own analysts approve actions.
questions.example: The customer pre-authorizes endpoint isolation, while account deletion needs specific approval.

options.label: Different approval by action, risk or system

questions.label: Can response follow the customer's processes?
questions.description: Include business-critical exceptions, change windows and approval chains.
questions.example: Production servers require application-owner approval even if workstation isolation is pre-authorized.

questions.label: What happens when work is escalated to the customer?
questions.description: Separate sending a ticket from tracking whether the issue was resolved.
questions.example: We retain the case owner, track customer tasks and verify the result before closure.

options.label: We retain ownership through verified resolution
Depends on the contracted activity; explain below

questions.label: How is feedback collected?
questions.description: Include mistakes, reopened cases and failed actions, not just satisfaction surveys.
questions.example: Analysts review corrected verdicts and a sample of automatically closed cases weekly.

options.label: Review of AI / automatically closed cases

questions.label: What is changed as a result?
questions.description: Select implemented changes, not improvements merely recommended to the customer.
questions.example: A corrected verdict updates a detection exception and a reviewed investigation procedure.

questions.label: Can customers see which improvements were implemented?
questions.description: A report of findings is different from a record of completed changes.
questions.example: The customer sees the change, case reference, approval, validation and deployment date.

options.label: Linked change, approval, validation and deployment record

questions.label: Can customers distinguish AI, automation and human work?
questions.description: Look for attribution for each decision or action, not an overall AI-powered label.
questions.example: The case timeline identifies the model-generated verdict, automated queries and analyst-approved containment.

questions.label: What happens when AI is uncertain or fails?
questions.description: Describe safe fallback, escalation and responsibility, not just model confidence.
questions.example: Conflicting evidence prevents auto-closure and routes the case to an analyst.

options.label: Escalates to a human with evidence
Falls back to bounded deterministic procedures
No AI in the evaluated service

questions.label: Which safeguards can you demonstrate?
questions.description: Select current controls and use the briefing to show evidence. These are declarations, not verified scores.
questions.example: Tool permissions prevent an investigation agent from taking response actions without approval.

options.label: Scoped tool permissions and approval controls
Testing malicious content in alerts and employee messages
Data residency, retention and tenant isolation

questions.label: What coverage and service commitments apply?
questions.description: State hours, escalation coverage, targets versus contractual SLAs, and exclusions for this package.
questions.example: 24/7 investigation; containment target measured from confirmed incident. Recovery is not included.
